In-memory map ranks first. Redis second. CDN third.

In-memory map gives lowest latency. It needs no network call. Data resets on restart. Use it when the service runs on one node and fits in RAM.

Redis adds shared state across nodes. It survives restarts. Network round-trip adds 1-5 ms. Run it when multiple instances read the same keys.

CDN pushes data to edge locations. It reduces origin load for global users. It fits static assets best. Dynamic keys and invalidation add complexity.

OAuth device flow ranks first. mTLS certs rank second. Long-lived PATs rank last.

OAuth device flow uses short-lived tokens plus refresh. It requires one browser step per login. It supports per-user revocation and audit logs. It fits CLI flows without storing secrets long-term.

mTLS certs bind identity to a private key. They need distribution and rotation for 40 users. They avoid tokens but add provisioning overhead.

Long-lived PATs grant static access. They need no extra steps at login. They stay valid until manual revocation and leak the entire credential on compromise.
